_readme: Append-only. Rows are appended by scripts/workflow-registry.py record and named by the release's prepare step (scripts/workflow-registry.py stamp); never edit or delete a row by hand. workflows/HISTORY.md is generated from this file.

build.note: The Build loop first written down as a step list of four phases and thirteen named steps, a description of the loop that nothing ran yet.
The Build loop now runs from this list: eleven steps, each its own step skill, and a stopped run resumes at the exact step it stopped on.

hotfix.note: A hotfix as a step list the runner can walk: the branch, the fix, its review, the merge into production and the deploy, each on the person's word.

plan.note: Planning as a named step list of twelve steps in five phases, with nothing created before the recorded sign-off and the approved drafts.

rebalance.note: Rebalancing a plan as a named step list of thirteen steps in five phases, each write needing the previous write's proof.

release.note: The full release as a step list for the default clearance scope, generated from one source with the other release definitions.

release-cut-to-deploy.note: The full release as a step list for clearance held from the cut to the deploy.
Every step of a release can be run, watched and re-run one at a time (shipped, not switched on yet).

release-docs.note: A partial release entry that runs only the documentation update.

release-merge-and-deploy.note: The full release as a step list for clearance held only to merge and deploy.
Every step of a release can be run, watched and re-run one at a time (shipped, not switched on yet).

release-notes.note: A partial release entry that writes only the release notes.

release-post-deploy.note: A partial release entry that runs only the post-deploy health check.
Every step of a release can be run, watched and re-run one at a time (shipped, not switched on yet).

approval.note: A workflow can stop for a person's approval (dormant until DevStride offers it).

auto-start.note: Decide whether the next release starts now (first published for the Release workflow).

branch.note: Create the item's branch from its working base (first published with the step contract catalog).

build.note: Build the item on its branch and hand back what was deferred, changed or dismissed (first published with the step contract catalog).

capture.note: File the follow-up work the build, the risk check and the review left untracked (first published with the step contract catalog).

checkpoint.note: A workflow step can run only when something is true, carry on past its own failure, or be done by a person (dormant until DevStride offers it).

ci-hold-proof.note: Prove pull-request CI waits for the ready flip before a release opens (first published for the Release workflow).

claim.note: Claim the item so no other session builds it at the same time (first published with the step contract catalog).

classify-at-checks.note: Classify the release again at the head the checks test (first published for the Release workflow).

classify-release.note: Say whether the release is light or full; anything unclear is full (first published for the Release workflow).

complete.note: Record the landed work on the item: its status, dates, links and claims (first published with the step contract catalog).

custom.note: A repository's own step: it passes, fails or holds, with evidence (first published with the step contract catalog).

deploy-approval.note: Approve the production deploy of one merge, only on the person's yes for that merge (first published for the Hotfix and Release workflows).

deploy-confirm.note: Confirm production serves the merge, or ask the person to confirm it (first published for the Hotfix and Release workflows).

dev-deploy-wait.note: Wait for the staging deploy of the release commit to be serving (first published for the Release workflow).

estimates-score.note: Score the estimates the shipped items carried (first published for the Release workflow).

ground-truth.note: Fetch both branches and read what other sessions landed (first published for the Release workflow).

hotfix-branch.note: Cut the hotfix branch from the production branch and push it (first published for the Hotfix workflow).

hotfix-catch-up.note: Merge a hotfix that reached production into the release branch (first published for the Release workflow).

hotfix-close.note: Close out the hotfix and say whether an open release branch must take it (first published for the Hotfix workflow).

hotfix-environment.note: Bring the local environment back to production code: a backward transition (first published for the Hotfix workflow).

hotfix-fix.note: Make the smallest change that fixes the production problem, then commit and push it (first published for the Hotfix workflow).

hotfix-merge.note: Merge the reviewed hotfix pull request into the production branch, only on the person's yes (first published for the Hotfix workflow).

hotfix-preflight.note: Check the working tree and name the hotfix branch from the repository's config (first published for the Hotfix workflow).

hotfix-report.note: Report the cut in one line and say what comes next (first published for the Hotfix workflow).

hotfix-stage.note: Name the environment this checkout deploys to, and stop before touching a production one (first published for the Hotfix workflow).

local-checks.note: Run the repository's local checks on the final tree and leave a receipt (first published with the step contract catalog).

plan-draft.note: Draft the specs for the signed-off shape; the drafting agents never write to DevStride (first published for the Plan workflow).

plan-draft-approval.note: Walk the person through the drafts until they approve them (first published for the Plan workflow).

plan-ground.note: Read what the plan already holds, read-only (first published for the Plan and Rebalance workflows).

plan-hand-off.note: Report the finished plan and where the build loop starts (first published for the Plan workflow).

plan-number.note: Number the leaves in the order the build loop will pick them (first published for the Plan workflow).

plan-orient.note: Resolve the plan root, its delivery profile and the organization's shape (first published for the Plan workflow).

plan-sign-off-record.note: Record the sign-off, and nothing else, in DevStride (first published for the Plan workflow).

plan-wire.note: Wire the dependency edges and prove no new leaf is left without one (first published for the Plan workflow).

production-in-branch.note: Merge production into the release branch when it is behind (first published for the Release workflow).

rationalize-gantt.note: Date the plan from its dependency graph, with the auto-scheduler off (first published for the Plan and Rebalance workflows).

rebalance-archive.note: Archive the originals only after their successors have edges (first published for the Rebalance workflow).

rebalance-gates.note: Check that nothing else is writing to the plan and the arguments are whole (first published for the Rebalance workflow).

rebalance-marker.note: Rewrite the plan root's delivery profile line, and only that line (first published for the Rebalance workflow).

rebalance-partition.note: Separate the leaves that may be re-sliced from the ones that are untouchable (first published for the Rebalance workflow).

rebalance-probe.note: Prove the auto-scheduler will not overwrite what the rebalance writes (first published for the Rebalance workflow).

rebalance-proposal.note: Propose the merges or splits and wait for 'yes, rebalance' (first published for the Rebalance workflow).

rebalance-renumber.note: Give each successor the number slot of its first absorbed item (first published for the Rebalance workflow).

rebalance-report.note: Report the re-sliced plan and the next item the build loop will pick (first published for the Rebalance workflow).

rebalance-rewire.note: Move every absorbed item's edges to its successor, adding before removing (first published for the Rebalance workflow).

rebalance-successors.note: Create each merged story with the original specs preserved (first published for the Rebalance workflow).

splice.note: Splice one story or defect into a live plan, wired and dated for the build loop (first published, for steps no built-in workflow names).
